detail: 1,440 days, one for every minute.

title: One day for every foot of the Empire State Building
detail: It stands 1,454 feet to the tip of its antenna.

title: As long as Michelangelo spent on the Sistine Chapel ceiling
detail: He painted it in about four years, from 1508 to 1512, mostly standing on scaffolding.

title: 1,500 days
detail: More than four years.

title: As long as light takes to get here from the nearest star
detail: Light from Proxima Centauri, the closest star after the Sun, takes about 4.2 years to reach us.

title: A Fibonacci number
detail: 1,597 is in the Fibonacci sequence, and it's a prime number too.

title: As long as it took to build the Golden Gate Bridge
detail: Work began on January 5, 1933, and the bridge opened on May 27, 1937.

title: One day for every meter in a mile
detail: A mile is about 1,609 meters.

title: As long as a deep-sea octopus mother guarded her eggs
detail: Scientists watched one guard her eggs for 53 months, the longest brooding known of any animal.

title: Golden days
detail: 1,618 days, like 1.618, the golden ratio found in shells and sunflowers.

title: A whole year on Ceres
detail: The dwarf planet Ceres, in the asteroid belt, takes about 1,680 days to go around the Sun.

title: A great gross
detail: 1,728 is a dozen dozen dozen: 12 × 12 × 12.

title: 1,729 days
detail: The famous "taxicab number": the smallest number you can write as the sum of two cubes in two different ways.

title: As long as Darwin's voyage on the Beagle
detail: The Beagle sailed from England in December 1831 and came home in October 1836.

title: One day for every yard in a mile
detail: 1,760 yards to the mile.

title: One day for every foot of One World Trade Center
detail: The tower is 1,776 feet tall, for the year of the Declaration of Independence.

title: As long as the Juno spacecraft's trip to Jupiter
detail: Juno launched in August 2011 and went into orbit around Jupiter on July 4, 2016.

title: One day for every poem Emily Dickinson wrote
detail: She wrote almost 1,800 poems. Fewer than a dozen were published while she was alive.

title: As long as it took to build the Hoover Dam
detail: Work ran from 1931 to 1936, about two years ahead of schedule.

title: 2,000 days
detail: About five and a half years.

title: 2,048 days
detail: Two to the eleventh power, the tile everyone's chasing in the game 2048.

title: As long as it took to rebuild Notre-Dame
detail: After the fire of April 15, 2019, the cathedral reopened on December 7, 2024. Rebuilt, and beautiful.

title: 50,000 hours
detail: Fifty thousand hours, about five and three-quarter years.

title: 300 weeks
detail: Three hundred weeks in a row.

title: One day for every game in Lou Gehrig's streak
detail: He played 2,130 games in a row. The record stood for 56 years.

title: As long as light takes to get here from Barnard's Star
detail: Barnard's Star, one of our nearest neighbors, is about 6 light-years away.

title: As long as it took to build the Burj Khalifa
detail: Work on the world's tallest building began in January 2004, and it opened in January 2010.

title: As long as Hayabusa2's round trip to an asteroid
detail: Japan's probe launched in December 2014 and brought a capsule of asteroid dust back to Earth in December 2020.

title: 2,222 days
detail: Four twos in a row.

title: As long as Galileo's trip to Jupiter
detail: The Galileo spacecraft launched in October 1989 and went into orbit around Jupiter in December 1995.

title: As long as it took to build the first railroad across America
detail: Work began in January 1863, and the golden spike joined the tracks on May 10, 1869.

title: One day for every mile of the Mississippi River
detail: The river runs about 2,340 miles from Minnesota to the Gulf of Mexico.

title: As long as MESSENGER's trip to Mercury
detail: The probe launched in 2004 and took more than six years of loops past Earth, Venus and Mercury to settle into orbit in 2011.

title: As long as the wait between America's two great eclipses
detail: The Moon's shadow crossed the US on August 21, 2017, and again on April 8, 2024.

title: As long as Cassini's trip to Saturn
detail: Cassini launched in October 1997 and reached Saturn on July 1, 2004.

title: 2,500 days
detail: Almost seven years.

title: A very divisible number
detail: 2,520 is the smallest number you can divide evenly by every number from 1 to 10.

title: As long as OSIRIS-REx's round trip
detail: The spacecraft launched in 2016, grabbed rocks from the asteroid Bennu, and dropped them off in the Utah desert in September 2023.

title: A Fibonacci number
detail: 2,584 is in the Fibonacci sequence: 987 + 1,597.

title: One day for every game in Cal Ripken Jr.'s streak
detail: He played 2,632 games in a row from 1982 to 1998, without missing one.

title: One day for every mile of the Pacific Crest Trail
detail: The trail runs about 2,650 miles from Mexico to Canada.

title: One day for every foot of the Burj Khalifa
detail: The world's tallest building rises 2,717 feet.

title: e days
detail: 2,718 days, like 2.718, the number e that shows up in growth and compound interest.

title: Four million minutes
detail: Four million minutes, more than seven and a half years of them.

title: 250 million seconds
detail: A quarter of a billion seconds.

title: Venus is back in the same spot
detail: Every eight years Venus shows up in almost the same place in our sky on the same date, tracing a five-petal pattern along the way.

title: As long as it took to build Tower Bridge
detail: London's famous bridge took eight years to build, from 1886 to 1894.

title: 100 full moons
detail: About a hundred cycles of the Moon, new moon to new moon.

title: As long as it took to go from "we choose to go to the Moon" to the Moon
detail: President Kennedy set the goal in May 1961. Apollo 11 landed on July 20, 1969.

title: 3,000 days
detail: More than eight years.

title: A number that shows up eight times
detail: 3,003 appears eight times in Pascal's triangle, more than any other number known except 1.

title: As long as it took to dig the Erie Canal
detail: Work began on July 4, 1817, and the 363-mile canal opened in October 1825.

title: As long as Voyager 2's trip to Uranus
detail: Voyager 2 launched in August 1977 and flew past Uranus in January 1986, the only spacecraft ever to visit it.

title: As long as Sirius's light takes to reach us
detail: Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky, is about 8.6 light-years away.

title: One day for every Calvin and Hobbes strip
detail: Bill Watterson drew about 3,160 strips from 1985 to 1995.

title: 3,333 days
detail: Four threes in a row.

title: As long as New Horizons' trip to Pluto
detail: The spacecraft launched in January 2006 and flew past Pluto in July 2015, 3,463 days later.

title: Five million minutes
detail: Five million minutes, about nine and a half years of them.

title: 500 weeks
detail: Five hundred weeks in a row.

title: As long as Hachikō waited
detail: After his owner died in 1925, the dog Hachikō went to the Tokyo train station to meet him every day for almost ten years.

title: As many days as there are seconds in an hour
detail: 3,600 days, one for every second.

title: About a whole new skeleton
detail: Your bones rebuild themselves slowly; the whole skeleton is replaced about every 10 years.

title: As long as it took the US to build the Panama Canal
detail: American work began in May 1904, and the canal opened in August 1914.

title: As long as Rosetta's chase of a comet
detail: The Rosetta probe launched in March 2004 and caught up with comet 67P in August 2014.

title: As long as it took to build the Suez Canal
detail: Digging began in April 1859, and the canal opened in November 1869.

title: 4,000 days
detail: Almost eleven years.

title: One whole sunspot cycle
detail: The Sun's activity rises and falls on a cycle of about 11 years.

title: 4,096 days
detail: Two to the twelfth power. Keep doubling 1 and you reach it on the twelfth try.

title: 100,000 hours
detail: A hundred thousand hours, more than eleven years.

title: A Fibonacci number
detail: 4,181 is the 19th Fibonacci number.

title: As long as Procyon's light takes to reach us
detail: Procyon, the bright star in the Little Dog, is about 11½ light-years away.

title: One day for every hit in Pete Rose's career
detail: Pete Rose got 4,256 hits, more than anyone in baseball history.

title: A whole year on Jupiter
detail: Jupiter takes about 4,333 Earth days, nearly 12 years, to go around the Sun.

title: As long as Tolkien spent writing The Lord of the Rings
detail: J.R.R. Tolkien worked on it for about 12 years.

title: As long as Voyager 2's trip to Neptune
detail: Voyager 2 launched in August 1977 and flew past Neptune in August 1989, the only spacecraft ever to visit it.

title: 4,444 days
detail: Four fours in a row.

title: As long as 13-year cicadas wait underground
detail: Some periodical cicadas spend 13 years underground before coming up into the sun, all at once.

title: One day for every square yard in an acre
detail: An acre is 4,840 square yards.

title: As long as it took to build the Brooklyn Bridge
detail: Work began in January 1870, and the bridge opened on May 24, 1883.

title: 5,000 days
detail: Almost thirteen and a half years.

title: 5,040 ways to line up
detail: Seven people can line up in 5,040 different orders.

title: As long as it took to carve Mount Rushmore
detail: Work ran from October 1927 to October 1941, about 14 years.

title: As long as Opportunity kept roving Mars
detail: Built for 90 days, the rover kept going from January 2004 to June 2018 and drove more than a marathon's distance.

title: One day for every foot in a mile
detail: 5,280 feet. You've walked a long way.

title: As long as it took to build the Sydney Opera House
detail: Planned for four years, it took 14. Work began in 1959, and it opened in October 1973.

title: As long as the Mir space station was in orbit
detail: Mir circled the Earth from February 1986 until March 2001.

title: 5,555 days
detail: Four fives in a row.

title: One day for every strikeout Nolan Ryan threw
detail: Nolan Ryan struck out 5,714 batters over 27 seasons, the record.

title: Half a billion seconds
detail: Five hundred million seconds.

title: 6,000 days
detail: More than sixteen years.

title: As long as Altair's light takes to reach us
detail: Altair, one of the stars of the Summer Triangle, is about 17 light-years away.

title: Kaprekar's number
detail: Take any four-digit number that isn't all one digit. Arrange its digits from biggest to smallest and smallest to biggest, and subtract. Keep going and you'll always reach 6,174.

title: As long as 17-year cicadas wait underground
detail: The longest-lived periodical cicadas spend 17 years underground before coming up into the sun.

title: One saros cycle
detail: Eclipses repeat in a cycle of about 18 years and 11 days. Ancient astronomers used it to predict them.

title: 6,666 days
detail: Four sixes in a row.

title: The 20th Fibonacci number
detail: Start with 1 and 1 and keep adding the last two: the 20th number you get is 6,765.

title: The Moon's phases are back on the same dates
detail: Every 19 years the Moon's phases fall on almost the same calendar dates again.

title: Ten million minutes
detail: Ten million minutes, about nineteen years of them.

title: 1,000 weeks
detail: A thousand weeks in a row.

title: About 700 million heartbeats
detail: And your heart has kept count of every one of them.

title: Jupiter and Saturn have lined up again
detail: The two giant planets meet in our sky about every 20 years. The last time was December 2020.

title: As long as it took to build the Great Pyramid
detail: The Great Pyramid of Giza is thought to have taken about 20 years to build.

title: 7,777 days
detail: Four sevens in a row.

title: 8,000 days
detail: Almost twenty-two years.

title: A perfect number
detail: 8,128 is the fourth perfect number. The next one is over 33 million.

title: 200,000 hours
detail: Two hundred thousand hours, almost twenty-three years.

title: As many days as there are hours in a year
detail: 8,760 days, one for every hour of a year.

title: 8,888 days
detail: Four eights in a row.

title: As long as Vega's light takes to reach us
detail: The bright summer star Vega is about 25 light-years away.

title: 9,999 days
detail: Five digits tomorrow.

title: 10,000 days
detail: More than 27 years.

title: About a billion heartbeats
detail: At roughly 100,000 beats a day, your heart has beaten about a billion times since day one.

title: As long as Nelson Mandela was in prison
detail: He was locked up for 27 years. When he came out in 1990 he helped lead South Africa to democracy.

title: As many days as there are minutes in a week
detail: 10,080 days, one for every minute of a week.

title: As long as the Berlin Wall stood
detail: The wall went up on August 13, 1961 and came down on November 9, 1989, after 10,316 days.

title: A whole year on Saturn
detail: Saturn takes about 10,759 Earth days, nearly 29½ years, to go around the Sun.

title: A billion seconds
detail: One billion seconds is about 31 years and 8 months.
12,321 reads the same forward and backward, and it's 111 times 111.

title: 12,345 days
detail: One, two, three, four, five.

title: As long as Voyager 1 took to leave the Sun's bubble
detail: Voyager 1 launched in 1977 and crossed into interstellar space on August 25, 2012, the first human-made object to get there.

title: As long as Arcturus's light takes to reach us
detail: Arcturus, the brightest star in the northern sky, is about 37 light-years away.

title: 20 million minutes
detail: Twenty million minutes, about thirty-eight years of them.

title: One day for every Broadway show of The Phantom of the Opera
detail: It played 13,981 times before closing in 2023, the longest run in Broadway history.

title: One day for every foot of Mount Whitney
detail: The tallest peak in the lower 48 states is 14,505 feet high.

title: 15,000 days
detail: More than forty-one years.

title: One day for every Peanuts comic strip
detail: Charles Schulz drew 17,897 Peanuts strips over almost 50 years, all by himself.

title: Fifty years
detail: Half a century, one day at a time.

title: One day for every foot of Kilimanjaro
detail: Africa's tallest mountain rises 19,341 feet.

title: 20,000 days
detail: Twenty thousand days. Nearly 55 years.

title: One day for every foot of Denali
detail: North America's tallest mountain is 20,310 feet high.

title: 25,000 days
detail: Twenty-five thousand days. More than 68 years.
